title: A Geiger counter loses counts at high rates
caption: With τ = 100 μs the counter reads m = n/(1 + nτ), which bends below the true rate n and can never exceed 1/τ = 10000 counts s⁻¹. A reading of 2000 counts s⁻¹ means the true rate is n = m/(1 − mτ) = 2500 counts s⁻¹: a fifth of the counts were missed.
alt: Measured rate against true rate: a curve that bends away from the straight no-loss line and levels off towards a dashed limit of 10 000 counts per second, with the point (2500, 2000) marked.
description: Non-paralysable dead time: n = m/(1 − mτ), so m = n/(1 + nτ).
Reading m = 2000 counts s⁻¹: mτ = 0.2, so n = 2000/0.8 = 2500 counts s⁻¹.
The dashed line m = n is a counter with no dead time.
However fast the source, m stays below 1/τ = 10000 counts s⁻¹.
